name: Vinati Organics Ltd
tagline: A stalled specialty-chemicals compounder showing real green shoots — ROCE and ROE both improved, valuation has actually de-rated to a more reasonable ~27x, and the DGTR issued a positive final finding on its anti-dumping case — but a sharp Q1 FY27 margin miss (24.5% vs 29.5% YoY) and still-weak 3-year sales CAGR (3%) mean the multi-year guidance-credibility gap isn't closed yet
business_overview: Vinati Organics manufactures specialty organic intermediates and monomers (ATBS, IBB, antioxidants, butyl phenols) for polymers, aromatics, and performance materials, serving domestic and export markets through long-term customer relationships. It is the world's largest ATBS producer (effective capacity ~40,000t of high-purity grades, running at 75-80% utilization).
fundamentals_table: Rs 13,587-13,869 Cr (roughly flat vs initial screen; down ~23% from a year-ago high)
P/E ~27-31x trailing (down from the community-flagged 42x), P/B 4.36x, EPS Rs 48.09
Consolidated PAT Rs 444 Cr (+9% YoY); CFO Rs 628 Cr, capex Rs 485 Cr, reported FCF ~Rs 491 Cr; dividend Rs 8.50/share (~20% payout)
Revenue -6.87% YoY to Rs 604 Cr (+13.78% QoQ); PAT +0.67% YoY to Rs 123 Cr — weak YoY print

Revenue growth reported inconsistently across sources (+4% to +28% YoY depending on standalone/consolidated basis); EBITDA margin contracted sharply to 24.5% from 29.5% YoY on rising input/energy costs — a real, not cosmetic, miss vs the 26-27% FY27 guide
fundamentals_narrative: Quality metrics have genuinely improved since the initial screen (ROCE 18.14%->21.4%, ROE 14.51%->16.2%, valuation de-rated from a community-flagged 42x to ~27-31x), and the company remains debt-free with strong cash generation (Rs 1,863 Cr cash, FY26 FCF ~Rs 491 Cr on Rs 444 Cr PAT). But the multi-year guidance-credibility gap the community flagged has not closed: 3-year sales CAGR is still only 3%, Q4 FY26 revenue fell 6.87% YoY, and Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin contracted sharply to 24.5% from 29.5% YoY on input/energy cost pressure — a real miss against the company's own 26-27% FY27 guidance. The one genuinely new positive this pass: DGTR issued a final finding confirming a positive, significant dumping margin and material injury from Chinese/Singapore antioxidant imports, moving the anti-dumping catalyst from 'pending investigation' to 'awaiting Ministry of Finance duty notification' — a real, not hypothetical, step forward.
technical_read: Not pulled this pass — no browser escalation triggered. Prior read: stock range-bound ~3.5-4 years, down ~23% from a year-ago high per current market-cap sourcing, consistent with the multi-year 'stalled execution vs guidance' pattern the community flagged.
sentiment_summary: Not re-read this pass — forum re-reading is vpscreen-scan's job, not deepdive-top100's. Reused the prior sentiment read: mixed-to-cautious, with 'still no sign of growth' complaints (most recent Jan 2026 post) despite harsh.beria93's detailed concall notes tracking genuine 30-40% YoY volume growth in newer lines (ATBS, antioxidants).

bse_notes: No SEBI/regulatory action found. DGTR issued final findings in the anti-dumping investigation (application filed by Vinati Organics) into 'certain Antioxidants' from China and Singapore: dumping margin found positive and significant, with material injury to the domestic industry confirmed — the case has moved from 'pending investigation' to a positive final finding, with Ministry of Finance duty notification the remaining step. No board/KMP/auditor changes, litigation, or pledge movements found in the last 6 months beyond routine FY26 results and the Rs 8.50/share dividend announcement. Promoter holding stable and high at 74.29% (Jun 2026), no pledge concerns identified.
bull_case: Genuine, measurable capital-efficiency improvement since the initial screen: ROCE 18.14%->21.4%, ROE 14.51%->16.2%, still debt-free with Rs 1,863 Cr cash and strong FCF generation (~Rs 491 Cr FY26, exceeding PAT)

The anti-dumping case against Chinese/Singapore antioxidant imports has cleared a major hurdle — DGTR's final finding confirms dumping and material injury — leaving only a Ministry of Finance duty notification before this becomes a real structural pricing tailwind

Valuation has actually de-rated to a much more reasonable ~27-31x trailing P/E (from the community-flagged 42x), and a reverse-P/E read shows the current multiple needs only ~14% EPS CAGR against a 15% FY27 volume guide — a modest, plausible bar if margins cooperate

Multiple new-product ramps remain real: ATBS Phase-1/2 capacity (~Rs 250-300 Cr combined capex, utilization already 75-80%), antioxidant/butylphenol segment growing from Rs 600 Cr (FY25) toward a guided Rs 800-850 Cr (FY26), and Veeral Organics (subsidiary) restarting production with revenue expected from Q3 FY27
bear_case: The core multi-year credibility gap the community flagged is still not resolved: 3-year sales CAGR remains just 3%, and Q4 FY26 revenue actually fell 6.87% YoY

Q1 FY27 delivered a real, not cosmetic, margin miss — EBITDA margin contracted to 24.5% from 29.5% YoY on rising input/energy costs, well below the company's own 26-27% FY27 guidance, raising fresh execution-risk questions rather than resolving old ones

Reported growth figures across sources for Q1 FY27 are inconsistent (+4% to +28% YoY depending on standalone/consolidated basis) — a data-quality flag that makes the recent trend genuinely hard to read cleanly, which this pass treats as 'lumpy' rather than a confirmed inflection

Even the improved 21.4% ROCE and 15% volume guidance describe a steady, mid-teens-growth specialty-chemicals compounder, not a hypergrowth setup — the box-score math permits a '10x' label but the underlying growth math does not credibly support one on a 2-3 year horizon

Veeral Organics' restart timeline is itself internally inconsistent across disclosures (October 2026 production resumption vs. a separately cited March 2027 commencement), adding uncertainty to that specific catalyst
verdict_headline: Real quality improvement and a genuine anti-dumping win, but growth math still doesn't support a multibagger label — a good business getting cheaper, not (yet) a 10x setup
verdict_reasoning: Four-box read: tailwind=yes (anti-dumping win + real new-product ramps), tam=weak (a mature, already-large-share ATBS franchise plus modest 15% guided volume growth doesn't describe an open-ended TAM), moat=yes (world's largest ATBS producer, established customer relationships), valuation=yes (multiple has compressed from a community-flagged 42x to ~27-31x, room to pay) -> score 3.5, which technically clears the >=3.0 bar for thesis_fit '10x-in-2-3-years'/'100x-in-10-years'.

Analyst override (same logic as applied to Nesco Ltd previously): a box score clearing 3.0 permits the return-magnitude label but does not mandate it when the underlying growth math doesn't support it. Here, 15% guided volume growth and a 3-year sales CAGR of just 3% describe a recovering quality compounder, not a company on a credible path to 10x revenue/earnings in 2-3 years or 100x in 10. thesis_fit is kept at 'neither' despite the box score.

This does not mean the name is uninteresting — the anti-dumping DGTR win, cheaper valuation, and improving ROCE/ROE are real, verifiable positives this pass, and Veeral Organics' restart plus ATBS Phase-2 capacity add genuine near-term catalysts. But Q1 FY27's margin miss (24.5% vs a 26-27% guide) shows the multi-year 'guidance not delivered' pattern the community flagged is not yet resolved.

Conviction held at Medium-High: the balance of a genuinely improving quality/valuation picture against a fresh, real margin disappointment and still-weak medium-term growth roughly offsets, leaving the net read unchanged from the prior pass.
